description:
Project: “Private observability minimum pack” (Private Deployment Automation: VPC + On‑Prem Packaging).

Goal
Deliver a baseline, supported observability bundle for Redwood Private installs (VPC and on‑prem) so operators get “day‑1 usable” dashboards, alerts, and log pipelines without bespoke work. The pack targets consistent signals across deployment modes and reduces support burden by standardizing what Redwood considers minimally required for a supported Private environment.

Scope (in)
- Packaged dashboards: inference API/gateway, runtime performance (prefill/decode), GPU utilization, error rates, saturation/queueing, routing/fallback behavior, control plane health, and installer/upgrade health.
- Packaged alerts: SLO-burn style alerts, high-urgency availability/latency/error alerts, resource exhaustion alerts (GPU/CPU/memory/disk), queue buildup, and log/metrics pipeline health.
- Log pipeline defaults: recommended collectors/agents (e.g., Fluent Bit/Vector), log formats, sampling/filters, and supported forwarding targets (customer SIEM, object storage, or managed log backend where applicable).
- Private constraints: air-gapped/on-prem packaging, constrained egress, customer-managed Grafana/Prometheus where required, TLS and auth defaults, RBAC/audit logging integration points.
- Documentation: operator install guide, configuration reference, troubleshooting/runbooks, and upgrade/rollback guidance.
- Validation: reference environments (VPC reference + on-prem lab), load test verification, alert tuning to reduce noise.

Scope (out)
- Fully bespoke customer-specific dashboards/alerts beyond the baseline.
- Long-retention analytics features (these remain Console/Telemetry roadmap items).
- Building a new observability backend; the pack integrates with supported, standard components.

Key stakeholders / teams
- Product (Private): Vivek Kulkarni (DRI), alignment on “supported” criteria.
- Eng Private Deployments + Pro Services: Markus Klein, Fatima Noor, Bruno Silva (customer install realities, packaging constraints).
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant (signals, SLOs, paging policy).
- Platform/Telemetry: Priya Natarajan / Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman (metrics semantics, pipelines).
- Security & Compliance: Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei (audit logs, secure defaults).
- Docs: Elliot Price / Kira Thompson (operator-facing docs).

Phases & timeline (typical ~10–12 weeks)
1) Discovery (2 weeks): gather requirements from recent Private installs/support escalations; decide supported backends and minimum signals.
2) Design (2–3 weeks): dashboards/alerts spec, metrics/log schema contracts, packaging approach for VPC vs on‑prem.
3) Implementation (4–5 weeks): repo work (dashboards, rules, charts/installer hooks), CI validation, golden signal tests.
4) Hardening + GA (2 weeks): noise tuning, runbooks, upgrade/rollback tests, release notes and handoff to Support/CS.

Deliverables
- Versioned “observability pack” bundle (dashboards + alert rules + log pipeline defaults) integrated into private installer/helm charts.
- Confluence operator docs + runbooks.
- Linear project plan and tracking.
- Supporting PRs across observability-pack, redwood-private-installer, redwood-helm-charts, and (small) redwood core changes.

Constraints
- Must work for both VPC and on‑prem (including air‑gapped); minimal external dependencies.
- Must be safe by default: avoid secrets in dashboards; secure endpoints; predictable RBAC.
- Keep alert noise low; prefer SLO burn alerts and pipeline health checks.
- Backwards compatibility for existing Private customers (feature flags / opt-in migration where needed).

files.description: Operator installation guide for the minimum pack in Private (VPC + on‑prem): prerequisites, supported components (Prometheus/Grafana/log forwarder), helm/installer steps, validation checklist, and common pitfalls.
Configuration reference: values.yaml/installer flags, dashboard import options, alert rule toggles, log filter/sampling knobs, TLS/auth integration points, and default retention guidance.
Day‑2 ops runbook: verifying collectors, triaging missing metrics/logs, dashboard troubleshooting, alert noise tuning workflow, and escalation paths.
“Supported install” checklist mapping required signals (metrics/logs/traces) to concrete queries and pass/fail criteria used by Solutions/SRE during go-live.
On‑prem packaging notes: image mirroring strategy, offline chart bundle layout, dependency pinning, and how to validate in an air‑gapped lab.
Reference architecture for VPC deployments: recommended topology for Prometheus/Grafana/log forwarding, network flows, and HA considerations.
Reference architecture for on‑prem: minimal footprint mode, optional HA mode, storage considerations, and integrating with customer SIEM/log backends.
Upgrade/rollback procedure for the pack: versioning policy, compatibility matrix with Private installer versions, migration steps, and rollback safety checks.
Catalog of included dashboards (names, purpose, target audience, required metrics/logs) and links to canonical queries/panels for each.
Alerting strategy doc: SLO definitions for Private, burn-rate alerting approach, severity mapping, default thresholds, and guidance for customer-specific tuning.
Standard defining required metric names/labels, log field schema, cardinality constraints, and “must-have” health signals for a supported Private deployment.
ADR covering which observability components are officially supported in the minimum pack (e.g., Prometheus rules format, Grafana provisioning, supported log forwarders) and why.
Security guidance: audit logging expectations around observability components (Grafana access, rule changes), secure defaults, and integration notes for regulated customers.
Working draft spec with open questions, component comparisons, early dashboard sketches, and links to relevant incidents/support tickets.
Spreadsheet-style doc: proposed alert rules, expected fire rates, staging/prod observations, and noise reduction decisions.
Test plan for air‑gapped validation: test matrix, required artifacts, step-by-step lab procedure, and pass/fail results table.
PRD draft: customer problem, definition of “supported,” success metrics (support ticket reduction, time-to-diagnosis), and rollout plan.
Rough dashboard wireframes and panel inventory (latency breakdowns, error panels, saturation) with notes on required metric instrumentation.
Linear initiative/PRD tracking issue: define “supported” Private observability minimum pack, include success metrics, rollout phases, and cross-team dependencies.
Create observability-pack repo structure for Private min pack: dashboard provisioning, alert rule layout, versioning, CI validation.
Implement Grafana provisioning for Private installer (dashboards + data sources), including secure auth defaults and config overrides.
Add PrometheusRule set for Private min pack: SLO burn alerts, pipeline health alerts, and resource exhaustion alerts; include unit tests/lints.
Log pipeline defaults: ship structured logs from gateway/runtime/control plane; define filters/sampling; support forwarding to customer SIEM.
Metrics contract work: ensure required labels exist (tenant/model/route), reduce cardinality risks, and document compatibility expectations.
On‑prem air‑gapped packaging: offline bundle build, image mirroring docs, and installer changes to consume the bundle.
Validation harness: automated smoke tests to verify dashboards load, alert rules parse, and required metrics/logs appear in a reference env.
Docs workstream: convert draft spec into Confluence install guide + runbooks; include troubleshooting tree and escalation guidance.
Add “supported signals” checklist output in installer (post-install report), including a command to run validation and export results.
Alert noise review + tuning: run rules against staging load, adjust thresholds, add suppression where appropriate, and define paging policy.
PR: Add initial dashboard provisioning framework (folders, naming conventions, variable templates) for Private minimum pack.
PR: Add gateway/service overview dashboard (RPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, 4xx/5xx, streaming disconnects) with consistent templating.
PR: Add runtime performance dashboard (prefill vs decode, queue depth, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate) and annotate cardinality constraints.
PR: Add GPU saturation dashboard (utilization, memory, throttling signals) and correlate with latency/error metrics.
PR: Add PrometheusRule bundle for SLO burn alerts and critical availability alerts; include promtool validation in CI.
PR: Add log pipeline health alerts (collector backlog/drops, export failures) and a “missing signals” alert group.
PR: Add dashboards for control plane services (config/policy store, auth integration health) relevant to Private ops.
PR: Add “Private install health” dashboard (installer/upgrade controller metrics, component readiness) and standard annotations.
PR: Wire observability-pack installation into Private installer (download/apply/provision steps) with version pinning and rollback safety.
PR: Add post-install validation command that checks required metrics endpoints, Grafana API reachability, and rule loading status.
PR: Support air-gapped bundle input (local artifact path) for dashboards/rules/logging configs; update CLI help and docs.
PR: Add optional Grafana provisioning hooks and ConfigMaps/Secrets layout for Private min pack (values.yaml-driven).
PR: Add PrometheusRule resources and allow rule group toggles per environment; add chart tests.
PR: Add templates/helpers for burn-rate alerts used by Private pack; document recommended SLOs and alert window pairs.
PR: Emit missing metrics needed by Private dashboards (e.g., route/model labels) and add guardrails to prevent high cardinality.
PR: Add structured logging fields for gateway/runtime to support customer SIEM routing (request_id/tenant/model/error_code) with redaction.
PR: Add lightweight “installer health” metrics endpoint consumed by Private install health dashboard and validation harness.
Thread coordinating SRE review of the proposed alert rules: paging policy, severity mapping, and initial feedback on noise risks.
Thread discussing metric label schema needed for dashboards (tenant/model/route) and how to keep cardinality under control.
Thread about on‑prem air‑gap constraints: image mirroring, offline bundles, and how the installer should locate artifacts.
Thread debating supported backends and integration patterns (Grafana provisioning vs customer-managed) leading into an ADR.
Thread reviewing security implications: Grafana auth defaults, audit logs for dashboard/rule changes, and least-privilege RBAC.
Thread where Support shares recurring Private customer pain points (missing dashboards, unclear alert thresholds) feeding the requirements list.
Thread coordinating doc ownership and information architecture for the install guide vs runbooks; requests for screenshots/examples.
Thread from an incident-like drill in a Private staging env where alerts failed to fire due to rule loading issues; includes triage steps and follow-ups.
Thread planning the release train for bundling the pack into the Private installer, including backport policy and customer comms timing.
Customer ticket: Private install lacks clear latency dashboards; requests recommended baseline panels and thresholds; includes environment details and support triage.
Customer ticket: Log forwarding from on‑prem cluster to SIEM dropping events; investigation notes, collector config snippets, and resolution/workaround.
Customer ticket: Alert rules not loading after upgrade; includes installer version, promtool errors, and links to a related GitHub hotfix PR.
Internal helpdesk: staging Private environment Grafana provisioning failing due to RBAC; request for fix and documented setup steps.
Internal helpdesk: request to add a standard “supported signals” validation checklist to internal runbooks for Solutions and Support.
Email thread (internal + select external prospects): clarifies what Redwood will call “supported” observability for Private, with timelines and scope boundaries.
Email thread with an enterprise prospect: collecting SIEM/log retention requirements and confirming whether the min pack satisfies their go-live checklist.
Security/compliance email thread: questions about auditing dashboard access/changes in Private environments and recommended control mappings.
Doc review email thread: shares draft install guide and runbook, requests reviews from SRE/Security/Solutions, and tracks requested edits.
Technical deep dive transcript with a regulated enterprise prospect focused on on‑prem constraints, SIEM forwarding, and what dashboards/alerts Redwood includes by default.
Security review transcript: customer questions about audit logging around observability tools, access controls, data retention, and evidence for compliance.
PoC check-in transcript: status on installing the min pack, issues encountered (rule parsing/log drops), and action items for Redwood and customer operators.
